UI button not clicked in a browser; image preview itself still needs a browser check.

items.title: Chat notifications (generic payload, mute-aware)
items.notes: New-message alerts go through the notification router: in-app by default, e-mail and webhook only if the person opts in, always generic (tested: no sender/title/text). Desktop alerts built. Mobile push is part of the deferred mobile work.

items.title: Realtime transport: long-poll + SSE + polling, seq replay, backoff
items.notes: Long-poll and SSE tested over the real routes; polling fallback is the plain sync route.

items.title: Chat API route set

items.title: Chat adversarial + security tests
items.notes: Adversarial coverage now complete: substitution, replay, rogue add/remove, stale epoch, cross-tenant, attachments, malformed/oversized, leakage, forged read events (clamped, per caller, outsiders refused) and replay by a removed participant (nothing served past the removal point, sends refused, later messages never decrypt).

items.title: Chat web UI (3-column) + browser verification
items.notes: 3-column UI works in a real browser (create, send, receive, reload restore). Group, attachments, contacts panel, mobile width still to verify.

items.title: Chat mobile screens + secure storage + biometric gate
items.notes: Mobile screens not started.

items.title: Chat desktop surface
items.notes: Desktop (inaya-desktop). Built and now RUN in the real desktop app against the live site (isolated profile): the native bridge works, chat opens, the 'Online' pill and 'This app is one device' show, the pop-out button opens a second chat window, and notify_chat_message / set_chat_unread return ok. Real-run bugs found and fixed: the site could not call ANY native command (no window.__TAURI__, every call refused by the access rules) and open_module_window hung (it was a blocking command). Needs a new desktop build/release to reach installed copies. Not observed: the toast on screen, the tray tooltip text, and the one-owner guard between two desktop windows.

items.title: Mobile push without plaintext (adapter)
items.notes: Mobile push notifications for chat. Part of the mobile work, which the owner deferred for now; nothing built.

items.notes: Request/accept/deny/cancel tested; contacts panel not browser verified.

items.notes: Remove/block/unblock tested.

items.title: Note types: text, rich, markdown, checklist, code

items.title: Note lifecycle: create/edit/rename/trash/restore/archive/delete
items.notes: Create, edit, autosave, trash/restore/permanent delete, retention purge (cron /api/cron/notes-purge), history list and restore verified (restore recovered a tampered latest version in the browser). Archive/pin/favorite logic tested; pin/archive buttons not clicked in the browser.

items.title: Note history + restore version
items.notes: Append-only history, restore as new version, revision bound to position by AAD (swap detected), newest 200 kept.

items.title: Pin, favorite, tags (create/rename/delete)
items.notes: Pin/favorite/archive/tags live in the encrypted per-user index with compare-and-set across devices. Browser: tag create/assign verified; pin, favorite, archive logic covered by tests.

items.title: Client-side encryption of private notes
items.notes: Server holds ciphertext only (verified in the DB and in the API response from the browser). Passphrase vault, per-note key sealed per participant, AAD-bound revisions. Not independently audited.

items.title: Note sharing, participants, read/write permission, conflict handling
items.notes: Share (read/edit), key rotation on removal, leave, explicit conflict panel, fingerprint pinning. Browser: share and remove (key v2) verified; the recipient side was verified by tests, not in a second browser session.

items.title: Note reference in chat
items.notes: Verified by hand in the browser only (attach from composer, encrypted send, Open link, deep link); no automated test yet.

items.title: Password-protected links
items.notes: Browser-verified 2026-10-04 on a production build: create link with password, wrong password refused, correct password opens v2 viewer. scrypt + lockout.

items.title: Share kinds: private, group, public, expiring, one-time
items.notes: Server logic tested against the real DB; max-openings counted in browser. Flag-gated (FEATURE_ADVANCED_SHARING, default off). Honest limit: view-only is a viewer mode, revocation cannot recall downloaded bytes.

items.title: Permission levels: view-only, upload-only, read/write, manage
items.notes: Server logic tested against the real DB; max-openings counted in browser. Flag-gated (FEATURE_ADVANCED_SHARING, default off). Honest limit: view-only is a viewer mode, revocation cannot recall downloaded bytes.

items.title: Max downloads, max expiry, IP / domain / device restriction
items.notes: Server logic tested against the real DB; max-openings counted in browser. Flag-gated (FEATURE_ADVANCED_SHARING, default off). Honest limit: view-only is a viewer mode, revocation cannot recall downloaded bytes.

items.title: Notify-on-access, watermark option, revoke any time
items.notes: Server logic tested against the real DB; max-openings counted in browser. Flag-gated (FEATURE_ADVANCED_SHARING, default off). Honest limit: view-only is a viewer mode, revocation cannot recall downloaded bytes.

items.title: Share manager (by me / with me / active / expired / revoked / pending) + delegate
items.notes: By-me list, create, status badge verified in browser; with-me / whole-org tabs and access-log dialog not clicked through.

items.title: Share access events + audit
items.notes: Server logic tested against the real DB; max-openings counted in browser. Flag-gated (FEATURE_ADVANCED_SHARING, default off). Honest limit: view-only is a viewer mode, revocation cannot recall downloaded bytes.

items.title: File request (secure upload link) create/revoke/expire
items.notes: Browser-verified 2026-10-04: owner creates request (passphrase), visitor uploads from public page, owner unlocks and saves; 2050 bytes round-tripped exactly. Sealed-box ECDH P-256 + HKDF + AES-256-GCM in browser.

items.title: File request public upload: limits, scan, classification hook, notify, audit
items.notes: Extension/risky-type/size/count/rate limits enforced and tested. Antivirus scan and classification hooks are NOT possible on end-to-end encrypted uploads; documented on the page and in the UI.

items.title: File request status + owner view
items.notes: Owner view shows count/expiry/uploader; filename hidden until passphrase unlock (verified in browser).

items.title: File lock/unlock/lease/force release/stale cleanup
items.notes: Browser: lock shown in document Share panel as mine with Renew/Unlock; atomic acquire, lease expiry, force-break, stale sweep covered by 9 tests.

items.title: Lock enforced in documents, S3/Azure, DirectSync
items.notes: Enforced at the S3/Azure store chokepoint (put/delete/lifecycle) and the new-version route (423). DirectSync now maps a server refusal for a locked, held or retention-protected file to a distinct BLOCKED state with the server's explanation (cargo tests 2/2), shown amber in the DirectSync view and retried with the failed files; the local file is never discarded. Not run against a real locked file from the installed desktop app.

items.title: Content metadata framework (typed fields)
items.notes: Typed fields, built-ins, sets, manager-only visibility, read-only system fields; saved from the document panel in the browser. Never exposed through share links.

items.title: Governance policy model: versioned, immutable after publish
items.notes: Versioned, immutable once published, second-admin approval, scope/precedence/dates, audit trail. Created and published from the UI in the browser.

items.title: Retention + archival + legal hold unified across file paths
items.notes: Published retention and legal-hold policies and the permanent class are enforced on delete, overwrite and lifecycle expiry; the daily governance-lifecycle job applies the period-end action (review: flag + tell administrators; archive; delete = hide like an S3 delete) for retention policies and archives inactive documents for archival policies, within each policy's scope, never touching held, locked or retention-locked objects, once per object per policy, through withJobRun. Not built: the deletion-approval requirement. Real database, 9/9 with retention tests.

items.title: Legal hold cannot be bypassed via S3/Azure/DirectSync
items.notes: The Business Workspace API has no destructive document route (the only DELETE removes a permission grant; the only removal is a reversible archive transition that touches no bytes), asserted by a scan test. S3/Azure store enforces holds at its chokepoint.

items.title: Classification engine: rules, patterns, PII, confidence, explanation
items.notes: Metadata, content, PII and term rules; highest sensitivity wins; explanation, confidence and rule versions recorded. Browser: rule suggested CONFIDENTIAL, accepted.

items.title: Classification history, manual override with reason
items.notes: History, suggestions, accept/reject, manual override with mandatory reason that blocks automation, explicit reclassification: all tested. Browser exercised history and accept; the override form was not clicked.

items.title: Client-side / customer scanner path for E2EE content
items.notes: Client verdict API validates rule ids and records source client; the evaluator is shared pure code. There is no browser or scanner UI that runs it yet, and no customer scanner agent.

items.title: AI-assisted classification through AI Security Gateway
items.notes: Goes through the existing docIntelligence classifyWithAi (AI Security Gateway), suggestion-only, confidence capped. Tested with an injected classifier; live model call not exercised.

items.title: DLP evaluator extension (IP, device, path, type, share type, counts)
items.notes: Every context field the SOW lists is matched by a pure evaluator. Browser: simulator and a live refused share open.

items.title: DLP actions incl. stronger auth, log-only, quarantine
items.notes: All six DLP actions are real. REQUIRE_STRONGER_AUTH: a person with an authenticator app confirms a fresh code (POST /api/orgs/step-up), opening a 10-minute window; wrong codes are limited and lock out, a used code cannot be replayed, someone without an authenticator is refused. The Business Workspace now shows an on-screen 'Confirm it is you' dialog when a request is refused for stronger authentication and retries once (browser-verified, including the no-authenticator message). Other parts of the app that call the server directly (not through the workspace helper) still show the plain error.

items.title: DLP wired to shares, downloads, uploads, S3/Azure
items.notes: Enforced on share creation/open/download (browser-verified live) and S3/Azure uploads and downloads (store level tested; the SigV4 routes were not exercised through a real S3 client).

items.title: DLP events + structured decisions
items.notes: Structured events with rule, policy version, masked IP; listed via the API in the browser.

items.title: Upload governance: ext/MIME/size/count, archives, bombs, hash lists
items.notes: Extension, MIME sniffing, size, volume, hash block list, zip bomb/nesting/entries/encrypted/unsafe path checks, all tested with real archives.

items.title: Antivirus adapter on all upload paths + quarantine
items.notes: Existing scanner (static checks, EICAR, optional ClamAV/Cloudmersive) runs on S3/Azure writes with quarantine-style refusal. End-to-end encrypted uploads can only get metadata checks. No external AV engine is configured in this environment.

items.title: Secure viewer modes + dynamic watermark
items.notes: Browser: restricted view with dynamic watermark (visitor, org, UTC time), context menu and copy blocked, blur hides content, watermark restored after removal. View-only mode shares the same code path; the share-link viewer (V2Viewer) was rewired to it but not re-run in a browser.

items.title: Session expiry, revocation, version pin, access log
items.notes: Short per-open views that expire, session expiry, immediate revoke, pinned document rows with explicit replacement, access log incl. viewer signals (seen in the browser log). The on-screen expiry wipe was tested by code path, not waited out.

items.title: Honest guarantee text; no plaintext derivative on server
items.notes: The guarantee text is on screen in the viewer and in the doc; no server-side plaintext derivative exists (decrypt happens in the browser).

items.title: Cloud-file ransomware signals + containment + rollback
items.notes: Signals, scoring with rule and confidence, tripwire, containment (writes refused through putS3Object), admin alert, evidence via the audit chain, resolve/lift and rollback planning verified. Rollback execution tested with a fake store only; no impossible-travel (no geolocation); suspect flag is per credential, not per user session; the existing resilience canary assets are not correlated.

items.title: Endpoint backup profiles, schedules, bandwidth, include/exclude
items.notes: Profiles (folders, include/exclude, schedule, bandwidth, version retention, mirror needs confirmation), pause/resume and client config verified in the browser and tests. The desktop app does not read these profiles or report runs yet.

items.title: Backup health, integrity verify, restore (original/alternate), recovery report
items.notes: Health states, integrity verification against stored objects, point-in-time restore plans, ransomware-safe approval flow and recovery report are tested (storage replaced by an in-memory fake). Restores are executed by the desktop client, which is not built; no real restore was run.

items.title: Device inventory
items.notes: Browser: this browser checked itself in, inventory and admin summary shown. Masked IP retention purge and device ownership tested. Desktop and mobile clients do not call the check-in yet.

items.title: Device policies + remote actions (revoke/block/re-auth/cache wipe/force sign-out)
items.notes: Browser: app-data wipe executed at check-in (marker cleared, device id kept); block ended the session at once. Trust policy and the central requireMembership gate tested. Wipe is application data only. Desktop/mobile clients do not obey commands yet.

items.title: Unified search tiers A/B/C with scope enforcement
items.notes: Tier B (permissioned enterprise content): names, paths, metadata, classification, your own tags, your shares and requests, data rooms for managers, and role-filtered pages; nothing the caller cannot open is returned. Tier A (E2EE notes and chat) is reported as local-only and is not implemented in the command palette; tier C (customer gateway index) is NOT_CONFIGURED. Document text is not indexed.

items.title: Preview PDF/Office/text/markdown/image/CSV (client-side for protected)
items.notes: Browser-verified on real encrypted files: PDF, XLSX, CSV, DOCX, PNG. Markdown renders through the component verified in Notes but its live room test hit a gateway miss; plain text/code, the workspace Preview button and legacy .doc/.xls were not verified.

items.title: DICOM viewer for Health (client-side)
items.notes: Browser: a real uncompressed 16-bit DICOM rendered with window/level sliders, patient name hidden by default. Compressed transfer syntaxes are refused honestly. Not a clinically validated viewer.

items.title: Microsoft 365/Graph adapter + secure open/edit flow
items.notes: Provider-adapter description with an honest status read from the existing Microsoft connection, edit sessions with a short-lived token, lock, base-version check and version verification, Office launch URIs. Sovereign by default: no file content goes to Microsoft and Office on the web is not offered. The desktop client that decrypts, launches Office and re-encrypts has not been updated to use sessions, and nothing was run against a live Microsoft 365 tenant.

items.title: Outlook secure-link insertion + share inspection
items.notes: Add-in manifest and task pane, secure-link insertion through the sharing engine (policy enforced, Manage access required), an e-mail block with expiry and reminders that never carries the password, link list, revoke and inspect (never reveals the token). Attachment-to-link conversion is NOT automatic. The add-in was never loaded in a real Outlook client; the manifest and files are checked for consistency only.

items.title: Office lock/versioning integration
items.notes: Edit sessions use the existing file locks and the existing versions route; finishing is accepted only for a real new version directly after the base. Control plane tested; end-to-end Office editing needs the desktop client and was not run.

items.title: Data Room 2.0: templates, NDA, per-section permissions, expiry, bulk
items.notes: Settings, sections, NDA gate (browser), per-section visitor scope, access expiry capped by the room, bulk add/update/remove, batch and group invites. Templates are the existing feature.

items.title: Data Room watermark, view-only, doc lock, final-version pin
items.notes: Watermark and view-only/download per document verified in the browser; lock, final-version pin and refused removal verified in the browser and tests.

items.title: Data Room visitor log, timeline, health, evidence package
items.notes: Visitor log (with viewer signals) and room health with warnings seen in the browser. Timeline, questions and the evidence package are tested server-side only; their UI tabs were not clicked.

items.title: Customer portal: files, forms, NDA, status, history
items.notes: Upload, download, secure form (answers encrypted at rest, reads audited) and hashed agreement items for one customer; status, notes, history and notifications; strict per-customer and per-organization isolation; real encrypted storage and real HTTP handlers tested; customer To-do flow checked in the browser. Uploads are single-request up to 4 MB. Customer SSO and real antivirus are as in the Customer Portal documentation (not verified live).

items.title: Sovereign Gateway agent: outbound-first, tenant-bound, signed upgrades
items.notes: Outbound-only agent: Ed25519 key made on the customer machine (private key stays there, encrypted with a passphrase), one-time enrollment token with proof of possession, every request signed with nonce and clock window, organization taken from the gateway record, revocation refused at the next request. The real agent ran over real HTTP against the real handlers and was seen ONLINE in the browser. Signed upgrade packages and rollback are implemented and unit tested; no release key or release pipeline exists yet, so no real upgrade has been delivered.

items.title: Connectors: filesystem, SMB, NFS; local scanner/index
items.notes: Filesystem connector with path-escape and symlink protection, metadata listing, bandwidth throttle, offline queue, resumable end-to-end encrypted transfer (restored byte for byte). The smb and nfs types use paths the operating system exposes (UNC path, CIFS or NFS mount); the agent does not speak those protocols. The local classifier applies simple extension and name rules and there is no local content index beyond the listing.

items.title: Deployment modes 1-3 explicit; mode 4 recorded only
items.notes: Modes 1 (cloud managed) and 3 (customer gateway) are real with computed readiness. Mode 2 is reported PARTIAL/NOT_CONFIGURED honestly: customer storage can receive backups but workspace documents still use Inaya-managed storage. Mode 4 (air-gapped) is recorded only, needs an explicit acknowledgement, and carries no claim.

items.title: Gateway health, queue, resume, revoke, audit, tenant isolation test
items.notes: Health (status, queue, lag, read failures), forwarded hash-chained audit with server-side verification and anchoring in the organization audit trail, queued commands, revocation, an offline alert once a day, a dashboard tile, and cross-tenant isolation tests (connectors, transfers, ACLs, administration). The hourly alert cron is configured in vercel.json and was not observed running on the deployment.

items.title: Network folders + NTFS/AD permission bridge + mapping health
items.notes: Real NTFS ACL reading through icacls (exercised on this Windows machine), NTFS ordering with deny preserved, group membership, exact-match identity mapping with confirm-first suggestions, enforcement that gives owners no back door, mapping health, conflict and stale diagnostics, change monitoring. Not done: a live LDAP/Active Directory source (not tested against a domain controller), per-file permissions (evaluated per approved folder), and visibility of access made directly on the customer network.

items.title: Site replication profile, lag, failover readiness, RTO/RPO evidence
items.notes: Active-passive replication profile; state, lag, backlog, RPO exposure, staleness, conflict and corruption measured from the backup engine's real replica records; recovery tests that read a sample back and verify its hash (sample-only timing, never extrapolated); named failover blockers; alerts; evidence package with hash. Recovery tests were exercised with in-memory provider stand-ins, not against the live storage providers. Failover is a manual operator procedure; no active-active behaviour is provided or claimed.

items.title: Government profile states (no certification implied)
items.notes: Four states, a technical-readiness profile only: live technical checks (met, not met, unknown), customer-specific authorization recorded by the customer and explicitly not verified, labels checked by a test not to imply certification. Choosing a state does not turn failing checks green.

items.title: NIST SP 800-53 control catalog + responsibility states
items.notes: 251 base controls across the 19 families as an internal curated catalog (not the NIST publication: no enhancements, no FedRAMP parameters) registered with the existing framework engine; implementation, responsibility, owner, evidence (vault, snapshot, link) and exceptions with mandatory expiry; evidence state is computed; live collectors never invent a pass; curated defaults labelled as defaults.

items.title: OSCAL-shaped evidence export
items.notes: OSCAL-shaped SSP plus every section the SOW lists, stable identifiers, linked evidence resources, SHA-256 and a structural self-check. NOT validated against the official OSCAL schema; vulnerability status is reported as not collected.

items.title: FIPS-ready crypto provider abstraction + inventory
items.notes: Provider registry, NIST-approved algorithm policy with a refusing fips_ready mode, known-answer vectors checked against two independent implementations, pairwise tests, usage and dependency inventories, FIPS status that never claims validation. Application code does not yet route its cryptography through the policy (it is a declared, tested abstraction and inventory), and no validated module exists.

items.title: Government audit profile + data labels
items.notes: Enhanced access records (user, role, department, object, action, time, device, masked address by policy, result, policy decision, authorization basis) written into the audit chain for every document read under a government profile, through the real retrieve route; government label set with neutral names for the customer-defined classes. Only the retrieve path is enhanced; other read paths keep their existing records.

items.title: Compliance readiness dashboard
items.notes: Readiness overview by family, evidence gaps, expired exceptions, live facts, government checks, cryptography and key status, all labelled readiness only. Not wired into the Admin Dashboard tiles.

items.title: Customer-managed key provider interface + local + KMS adapter + rotation
items.notes: Provider interface with platform, local and AWS KMS providers; envelope re-wrap of the server-managed layer's data key (platform copy removed); tenant, purpose and environment binding; rotation with versions and retired state; disable switch; operation audit and failure telemetry with no key material. KMS was tested against a stand-in implementing the AWS protocol (real AWS SDK client, authenticated EncryptionContext), NOT a live AWS account. Applies to server-managed storage only; client-side encrypted content is outside it by design.

items.title: Org branding, legal text, domains, email templates (sanitized)
items.notes: Logo, favicon, background, title, accent, support URL, terms/privacy text and email header/footer are validated (real image magic bytes, size caps, https URL, plain text only) and shown on share, file-request and data-room pages (share and request pages checked in the browser). Branded email builder escapes everything. Custom domain: TXT ownership challenge is real and verified with an injected resolver; routing the domain to Inaya is NOT configured and is reported as NOT_CONFIGURED.

items.title: Tenant isolation hardening + automated scanner tests per new route group
items.notes: Static scanner over every route group added by the SOW (session or key auth before data access, org id from the session/record, never the body) plus the per-feature cross-tenant tests. Heuristic: it checks structure, it is not a proof; found no gaps.

items.title: Role gates: security/storage/compliance/helpdesk/VDR/device admin
items.notes: Additive adminRoles on org_members; owner/admin hold every scope, auditor reads only. Applied to governance, DLP, devices, ransomware, backup, webhooks, data rooms and dashboard. In the browser a deviceAdmin read devices (200), was refused DLP (403) and could not grant themselves roles (403).

items.title: Admin dashboard with honest NO DATA states
items.notes: 19 tiles computed from real records; OK, ATTENTION, NO_DATA, NOT_ENABLED and UNKNOWN states each explained. S3/Azure request usage is UNKNOWN because request counts are not collected; DirectSync run status is not reported to Inaya.

items.title: Smart notifications: events x channels, privacy-safe bodies
items.notes: 16 events x in-app/email/push/desktop/webhook with per-person preferences; email, push and webhook carry generic text only, the in-app feed keeps detail; share-expiry job notifies once. Fixed a real bug found by the tests: event names contain dots, which Mongo read as nested paths, so a saved preference was never applied. Push is NOT_CONFIGURED (no push credentials); the desktop channel is the same feed the desktop app already reads; email was tested with a stub sender, not a live mailbox in this pass.

items.title: Public/API-key route families (shares, file-requests, governance, devices, classification, compliance, evidence)
items.notes: Shares, file requests, governance, DLP events, classification, devices and endpoint backup health, org bound to the key, feature flags honoured, same document-access and expiry checks as the app (tests found and fixed a missing check in the first version). Tested by calling the route handlers with a real key against MongoDB; not exercised over HTTP. File request creation, chat, contacts and notes are intentionally not offered.

items.title: SDK namespaces Chat/Contacts/Notes/Shares/FileRequests/Governance/Devices/Compliance
items.notes: Shares, FileRequests, Governance, Devices, Compliance and Webhooks.verify added. Chat, Contacts and Notes wrappers are intentionally not provided: those are end-to-end encrypted in the client and cannot be a Bearer-key REST wrapper. Not yet released as a new SDK version.

items.title: CLI commands chat/shares/file-request/device/governance/backup
items.notes: shares, file-requests, devices, governance and backup command groups using an API key only. No chat, notes or contacts commands (E2EE) and no file-request creation; never reads a wallet key. Tested in-process through commander against a stand-in server; the packaged CLI was not run end to end.

items.title: General signed webhook registry: rotate, pause, replay protection, DLQ, redeliver
items.notes: Signed (HMAC-SHA256 over t.body), SSRF-refused, retries 1/5/15/60/240/720 min then dead letter, auto-pause after 20 failures, 24h secret rotation grace, content stripped, chat metadata opt-in; real HTTP round trip tested; UI create/rotate checked in the browser. Emitters cover object, share, file request, DLP, backup, ransomware, device, workflow, resilience and chat-metadata events; identity events are not emitted. The every-minute delivery cron is configured in vercel.json and was not observed running on the deployment.

items.title: Read-only AI governance helpers via guarded execution
items.notes: Seven read-only tools (policies, DLP summary and explanation, classification counts, ransomware status, device summary, backup health) registered with the OS router; role re-checked per tool; requests to change anything or to certify compliance are refused; no file content is returned. Exercised by tests calling the tools and checking the router wiring; not run against a live model in this pass.

items.title: File triggers (upload, classification, share, expiry, hold, DLP, VDR, backup failure)
items.notes: Emits file.uploaded, upload_blocked, classified, classification_suggested, dlp_blocked, shared, share_opened plus (new) share_expiring, legal_hold_changed, vdr_accessed and backup_failed at their real emission points. The new four are covered by a constants test only; a live workflow run on them was not exercised.

items.title: File actions (tag, approval, lock, retention, move, evidence, ticket, resilience test)
items.notes: action.file_governance now does classify, set_metadata, revoke_shares, set_retention, lock and unlock (tested, permission checked, no delete). Ticket and approval already exist as nodes. Not built: tag (the metadata framework has no org-level tag field) and move.

items.title: File management UX: list/grid, favorites, pins, tags, recent, shared, locked, hold, classification
items.notes: List and grid, filters (all, favorites, pinned, recent, shared with me, locked, legal hold, classification, tag), favorites, pins, personal tags and recents, classification/lock/hold badges; checked in the browser against seeded documents.

items.title: Business Workspace navigation grouping + command palette entries
items.notes: Admin Dashboard and Webhooks in the navigation by role; the command palette finds documents, shares, requests and pages and the chat history this device holds (browser-verified: a sent message was found, shown as 'Secure Chat - this device'). Notes are not searched from the palette: they are end-to-end encrypted and locked until opened.

items.title: Mobile: contacts, notes, shares, upload requests, notifications, offline cache, camera upload, device state
Desktop: chat, notes, locking, endpoint backup, device inventory, smart-sync indicators
items.notes: Chat, notes, locks, endpoint backup, device inventory, gateway views and the secure viewer run inside the desktop window because it hosts the web app; DirectSync, Drive mount, secure links and tray existed. Added: chat window, chat alerts, unread tooltip, cache and device controls, sign-out policy, offline indicators, DirectSync BLOCKED state. A real run in the desktop app found and fixed a pre-existing blocker (the site could not call any native command) so these features can work once a new build is released. NOT built: smart-sync placeholder files.

items.title: Performance targets: chat ack, pagination, bounded dashboards
items.notes: Chat send path cut from about 17 to about 8 sequential database round trips (acknowledgment itself about 5); measured p95 1.7 s for the whole path at a 200 ms database round trip (3.4 s before); every list endpoint caps page size; dashboard tiles over event data use grouped counts (6000 rows, exact). Not measured: chat history paging and local search in the client, any production-scale load.

items.title: Background jobs: idempotent, retry, stale-run, tenant scoped
items.notes: withJobRun: atomic lease (partial unique index), stale takeover, bounded backoff retries, redacted failures, minimum interval, tenant scoping; the four crons added by this SOW run through it. Crons that existed before the SOW were not rewired. 8/8 against the real database.

items.title: Privacy-safe metrics for chat/storage/gateway/compliance
items.notes: Fixed-catalog counters, live gauges, org endpoint, platform Prometheus export, client reporter, and a Usage panel on the Admin Dashboard (browser-verified: counters and the privacy line show).

items.title: All SOW documentation set + docs site/API/SDK/CLI reference updates
items.notes: Every document the SOW names exists; docs-site API (12 new endpoints, regenerated OpenAPI), SDK and CLI references and a Secure Collaboration product page were added; docs tests 10/10.

items.title: Unit + real-DB + security + integration + browser verification
items.notes: Final run 2026-10-05: 20 suites / 189 tests against the real database (chat x3, devices, gateway x2, governance x3, sharing x3, notes, keys, compliance, metrics, phase8, jobs, tenant scan, performance): 184 passed, 5 chat-routes failures traced to my own browser-check cleanup deleting live test orgs mid-run; chat-routes re-run alone 8/8. Not every item has a browser pass; see per-item rows.

items.title: Additive migrations, dry-run, flags, rollback plan
items.notes: Dry run and --apply run against the dev database: 82 collections referenced, all additive; index setup is lazy per module and --apply warms five modules (others create theirs on first use); every flag unset by default. Rollback is a flag switch, documented; nothing is dropped by the script.

items.title: Final verification report + honesty checklist
items.notes: Report written with the 20 required parts and the section 59 checklist. It states that mobile and desktop surfaces are not delivered, which is why the SOW as a whole is not complete.
